ai_root_cause: VLAN30 SVI (interface Vlan30) is administratively down.
ai_evidence: show ip interface brief shows Vlan30 status = administratively down.
ai_fix_steps: interface vlan30 -> no shutdown.

ai_root_cause: Trunk between SW1 and SW2 is not configured, so VLAN10 traffic never crosses.
ai_evidence: CDP message references Gi0/1 on both switches.
ai_fix_steps: Re-enable trunking with switchport mode trunk on both ends.

ai_root_cause: PC1 has the wrong default gateway configured (192.168.10.254 vs router's 192.168.10.1).
ai_evidence: PC ipconfig gateway differs from R1 Gi0/0 IP in show ip interface brief.
ai_next_command: show ip interface brief on R1
ai_fix_steps: Reconfigure PC1 (or DHCP scope) with gateway 192.168.10.1.

ai_root_cause: Gateway interface Gi0/1 on R1 is down, cutting off all of VLAN20.
ai_evidence: show ip interface brief: Gi0/1 status/protocol both down.
ai_fix_steps: Check cable/SFP, then no shutdown on Gi0/1 if administratively down.

ai_root_cause: Duplicate IP address conflict on the gateway address 192.168.30.1.
ai_evidence: %IP-4-DUPADDR syslog message names 192.168.30.1.
ai_fix_steps: Locate and reconfigure the rogue device using 0050.7966.6802; remove the static/duplicate IP.

ai_root_cause: Gateway interface on R1 is physically down, so HSRP can't fail over.
ai_evidence: show standby brief output shows an unusual state.
ai_next_command: show ip interface brief on R1
ai_fix_steps: Check R1's physical interface and cabling.

ai_root_cause: DHCP pool VLAN10 is exhausted (10/10 addresses leased).
ai_evidence: show ip dhcp pool: Leased addresses = 10, Total addresses = 10.
ai_fix_steps: Enlarge the pool or shorten the lease time; check for stale bindings to clear.

ai_root_cause: VLAN20 SVI has no ip helper-address, so DHCP broadcasts never reach the server in VLAN10.
ai_evidence: show running-config interface vlan20 shows 'no ip helper-address'.
ai_fix_steps: Add ip helper-address <DHCP-server-IP> under interface vlan20.

ai_root_cause: DHCP pool VLAN10_POOL is exhausted.
ai_evidence: Pool configuration was reviewed.
ai_fix_steps: Increase pool size.

ai_root_cause: Excluded-address range 192.168.40.1-192.168.40.254 leaves no addresses for DHCP clients.
ai_evidence: show run | include excluded shows the full host range excluded.
ai_fix_steps: Narrow the excluded range to only the addresses actually reserved (e.g. gateway, AP management IPs).

ai_root_cause: PC3 is configured with a public DNS server (8.8.4.4) that has no record for the internal name server.local.
ai_evidence: ipconfig /all shows DNS Server: 8.8.4.4; internal DNS server is 192.168.10.5.
ai_fix_steps: Point PC3 (or the DHCP scope) at the internal DNS server 192.168.10.5.

ai_root_cause: Extended ACL 101 denies UDP port 53, blocking DNS.
ai_evidence: show access-lists 101 line 10: deny udp any any eq 53.
ai_next_command: show ip interface gi0/0 | include access list
ai_fix_steps: Remove or edit ACE 10 in ACL 101, or add a permit above it for the DNS server's IP.

ai_root_cause: webserver.local has a stale DNS record pointing to 192.168.10.99 instead of .50.
ai_evidence: show hosts entry for webserver.local lists 192.168.10.99.
ai_fix_steps: Update/re-register the host entry for webserver.local to 192.168.10.50.

ai_root_cause: VLAN30 DHCP pool has no dns-server line, so clients get no DNS server.
ai_evidence: show run | section VLAN30_POOL has no dns-server statement.
ai_fix_steps: Add 'dns-server <IP>' to the VLAN30_POOL configuration.

ai_root_cause: R1 has no route to the branch subnet 10.10.20.0/24.
ai_fix_steps: Add a static route (ip route 10.10.20.0 255.255.255.0 <next-hop>) or enable a routing protocol toward BR1.

ai_root_cause: OSPF neighbor never forms because BR1's interface is in area 1 while R1's is in area 0.
ai_evidence: show ip ospf neighbor returns nothing; show ip protocols shows area 1 on BR1's WAN network.
ai_fix_steps: Match the area ID on both sides of the WAN link (both should be area 0, or whatever the design calls for).

ai_root_cause: Duplicate IP conflict is preventing the new PC from communicating.
ai_evidence: New PC (192.168.10.200) can't reach anything on the subnet.
ai_fix_steps: Check for another device using 192.168.10.200 and reassign one of them.

ai_root_cause: Static route to 172.16.5.0/24 has a next-hop (192.168.99.99) that isn't reachable, so the route never installs.
ai_evidence: show ip route 192.168.99.0 returns '% Network not in table', confirming the next-hop can't be resolved.
ai_fix_steps: Correct the next-hop IP, or reference the correct exit interface instead of an IP.

ai_root_cause: Standard ACL 10 (outbound on Gi0/2) denies the 192.168.10.0/24 source subnet.
ai_evidence: show access-lists: ACL10 line 10 denies 192.168.10.0/0.0.0.255; ACL10 is set outbound on Gi0/2.
ai_next_command: show ip route; show access-lists; show interfaces trunk
ai_fix_steps: Add a permit line above the deny for the required traffic, or remove ACL10 from Gi0/2 if it's not needed there.

ai_root_cause: ACL 5 on the VTY lines only permits 192.168.10.50; the admin's new IP isn't listed.
ai_evidence: show access-lists 5 has a single permit line for 192.168.10.50.
ai_fix_steps: Add 'permit 192.168.10.100' to ACL 5 (or replace the old entry if the admin's IP changed permanently).

ai_root_cause: No ACL is applied to Gi0/3 at all, so guest traffic isn't isolated.
ai_evidence: show ip interface gi0/3 confirms both inbound and outbound access lists are 'not set'.
ai_fix_steps: Create and apply an ACL on Gi0/3 that denies guest VLAN traffic to internal server subnets, permits internet-bound traffic.

ai_root_cause: ACL 110 is blocking Telnet to the server (192.168.10.50).
ai_evidence: show access-lists 110 shows a deny tcp line targeting the server.
ai_fix_steps: Remove ACL 110 from the interface to restore access.

ai_root_cause: Gi0/1 is missing 'ip nat inside', so no traffic is ever marked for translation.
ai_evidence: show ip nat translations is empty; show run confirms Gi0/1 has no ip nat inside line.
ai_fix_steps: Add 'ip nat inside' under Gi0/1 (the VLAN10-facing interface).

ai_root_cause: The static NAT entry has a typo - maps to 192.168.10.8 instead of 192.168.10.80.
ai_evidence: show run | include static shows 'tcp 192.168.10.8 80 ...' vs the real server IP 192.168.10.80.
ai_fix_steps: Remove the incorrect static NAT line and re-add it with 192.168.10.80.

ai_root_cause: ACL 1's wildcard mask (0.0.0.15) only covers a /28, not the full /24 VLAN10 subnet.
ai_evidence: show access-lists 1: permit 192.168.10.0 wildcard bits 0.0.0.15.
ai_fix_steps: Change the wildcard mask to 0.0.0.255 to cover the full /24 subnet.

ai_root_cause: WLAN 1 is mapped to the 'management' interface instead of the employee-data VLAN.
ai_evidence: show wlan 1 lists Interface: management.
ai_fix_steps: Change WLAN 1's interface mapping to employee-data under the WLC's WLAN config.

ai_root_cause: WPA2 passphrase mismatch is causing authentication failures for some clients.
ai_evidence: Multiple clients failing to authenticate to the same SSID.
ai_fix_steps: Re-push the correct WPA2 passphrase to affected clients.

ai_root_cause: AP-EastWing has lost its connection to the WLC (Disassociated state).
ai_evidence: show ap summary: AP-EastWing State = Disassociated, all other APs = Registered.
ai_next_command: show cdp neighbor detail on the EastWing switch port
ai_fix_steps: Check the switch port, PoE budget, and cable feeding AP-EastWing; re-seat/replace as needed.

ai_root_cause: VLAN10 is missing from the trunk's allowed-VLAN list on Gi0/1.
ai_evidence: show interfaces trunk lists allowed vlans as 1,20,30 - no 10.
ai_fix_steps: switchport trunk allowed vlan add 10 on Gi0/1 (both switches).

ai_root_cause: Fa0/3 is in the wrong VLAN (default VLAN1 instead of VLAN10).
ai_evidence: show vlan brief lists Fa0/3 under VLAN1; running-config confirms switchport access vlan 1.
ai_fix_steps: On SW1: interface fa0/3 -> switchport access vlan 10.
